lesson: Run 7's binding fix is too narrow: bindPendingPermissionInteractionMessage finalizes eligible=false for a batch ONLY when the rendered decisionOptions include a remember code. The contract (ruling 3, AC2) says EVERY coalesced batch ends ineligible: a batch member whose context is provisionally eligible must be set eligible=false whether or not a code is rendered (today no card renders codes, so the current condition never fires, and a forged remember code on a batch card would learn). Fix: drop the decisionOptions condition — for matchKind === 'batch', update every member that carries a parseable rememberContext to eligible=false; members without a context are untouched (no update call, today's path). Keep individual prompts exactly as they are (no update). Add the batch case to the durability suite's context round-trip leaf (a batch binding turns an eligible context ineligible; a batch without contexts makes no update call). Then re-run the 12 leaves, tsc, check:architecture, prettier. Do not run npm test in the sandbox (EMFILE); the host runs it.
